description_full: Endeavour Silver Corp., a silver mining company, engages in the acquisition, exploration, development, extraction, processing, refining, and reclamation of mineral properties in Mexico, Chile, Peru, and the United States. It primarily explores for gold and silver deposits, and precious metals, as well as polymetals. The company was formerly known as Endeavour Gold Corp. and changed its name to Endeavour Silver Corp. in September 2004. Endeavour Silver Corp. was incorporated in 1981 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (7/10).
financial_summary: Endeavour Silver Corporation is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $2.3B market cap on $468M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +31% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $102M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -15.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sector_headwinds.text: Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Piotroski score 4/9 — below the median for a healthy business

Cyclical sectors like Basic Materials tend to underperform in slowdowns
Late-cycle dynamics increase the probability of a slowdown
Commodity price volatility and cost-curve position — in a downturn only the lowest-cost producer has a business, and the rest carry the overhead.
Environmental remediation liability — tightening regulations on emissions, tailings, and water use create open-ended balance-sheet risk that grows with each legislative cycle.
Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sect: Its 8% operating margin is roughly in line with the Basic Materials median (10%).

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 18% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 14% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 48% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 77% and a beta of 1.13, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 3.21 vs 5y 1.32), so read it loosely.
About $68.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 54% in the 2020 crash, 55% in the 2022 bear market and 82% in 2008.
val: On multiples it looks expensive against Basic Materials peers: P/E 39.2 vs 16.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 12% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -4.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $15.50 on average, 98% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.3%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
It runs a 19% gross margin and burns cash (FCF margin -22%).
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only -0.57x and high accruals (-15.1% of assets).
Operating margin is running 8pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $202.7M.
The Beneish M-score (-2.13) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 30.5% over 3 years and 27.6% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 38%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 6.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 59%.
The share count has grown 10.7% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 2,160 employees, each generates about $216K of revenue, 0.3x the Basic Materials median, and productivity has risen 15.2% a year.
